seo.metaDescription: ChartsProvider sets the locale and currency; useChart, useFormat and useRegisterPoints let you draw your own marks.

props.markdown: `BarChart` and `LineChart` read their number formats from a provider, and a mark of your own can do the same. This page covers `ChartsProvider`, which sets the locale and currency for everything inside it, and the three hooks you need to draw something the library does not: `useChart`, `useFormat` and `useRegisterPoints`.

Put `ChartsProvider` once near the top of the page. `locale` is a BCP 47 tag and `currency` an ISO 4217 code. Every chart, `Stat`, `Meter` and axis below it formats numbers, dates and currency that way, so the same data reads naturally for each audience. Without a provider the defaults are `en-US` and `USD`.

The `Stat` and both charts share one provider: thousands are separated with a dot, the decimal separator is a comma and the euro sign follows the number. Nothing is passed to the charts except `format="currency"`. The props are plain values, so this example also renders in a Server Component; see [Getting started](/docs/getting-started) for the charts used here and [LineChart](/docs/line-chart) for series.

When none of the building blocks in [Composition](/docs/composition) draws what you need, write a component and put it inside `Chart`. `useChart()` returns the size, the margins, the data, the number formatter, the active point and the `x` and `y` scales (narrow them on `kind`: `'linear'`, `'band'`, `'point'` or `'time'`), `useFormat()` returns formatters in the provider's locale, and `useRegisterPoints()` tells the chart where your points are.

Lollipops are not a built-in mark. `Lollipops` reads the scales with `useChart()`, labels each point with a formatter from `useFormat()`, and registers the points. That registration is what makes `NearestPointer` find them under the pointer, `Tooltip` show them and the arrow keys walk them. Focus the chart and press `Home` to hear the first one.

**Memoize the points you register.** `useRegisterPoints(points)` registers again every time the array changes identity, so build it in `useMemo` with the scales and formatter as dependencies. Each point needs a unique `id`, an `index`, the `datum`, a position in plot pixels (`x`, `y`), a `label` for screen readers and the tooltip `segments`. Hooks cannot run in a Server Component, so a file that uses any of them starts with `'use client'`.

props.text: Several React roots on one page

props.markdown: Pattern ids, for hatching and gradients, come from React's `useId`, which is only unique within one root. When charts render in separate roots (islands, micro-frontends), two charts can end up with the same pattern id. Give each chart its own `chartId`. `Chart`, the high-level charts and `Heatmap` take it.

props.code: <BarChart chartId="margin-chart" data={weeks} x="week" y="margin" title="Margin by week" />
